native_result.query: What is the proportion of junior professors in replicated studies in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, replicated studies have a much higher proportion of junior professor (64.7%) and in the original studies the senior professors are more represented (82.4%)
native_result.HypoB: Assuming a seniority hierarchy that the dataset itself does not define (Professor > Associate Professor > Assistant Professor > Assistant > Researcher) and counting 'junior professor' as Assistant Professor or Assistant - i.e. the assistant level, with Researcher excluded as non-professorial - roughly two in five of the replicated studies in Psychology were led by a junior professor: among all 97 original-replication pairs of the Psychology replication project (project == 'rpp', all with usable seniority) 38 have a junior most-senior author on the replication line (seniority.r), i.e. 38/97 = 39.2% (Wilson 95% CI 30.1%-49.1%) - a share that rises to 16/35 = 45.7% (CI 30.5%-61.8%) if one restricts to the studies that additionally replicated successfully (replicated == 1) - whereas on the original-study line (seniority.o) not one of the 97 has an assistant-level lead (0/97 = 0%; 5/97 = 5.2% if Researcher is also counted as junior), because the replicated originals were overwhelmingly full professors (83/97), so the junior-professor share is a property of the replication teams rather than of the original papers.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded File A (meta-regression_study_data_...csv, 927x57) and File B (meta-regression_replication_success_data_...csv, 143x15). 2) Excluded study-level roll-ups (aggregated == True; 26 rows, ml1/ml3 only) to avoid double counting -> 901 rows. 3) Primary population: project == 'rpp' (Psychology project) = 97 rows, 97 unique ids, one row per O/R pair; seniority.o and seniority.r 0% missing, so N = 97. 4) Numerator: seniority.r in {Assistant Professor, Assistant} (junior definition D2, tier order assumed) = 38 -> 38/97 = 39.2%, Wilson 95% CI 30.1-49.1%. 5) Parallel column seniority.o (D1/D2 = 0/97; D3 with Researcher = 5/97) plus seniority.o x seniority.r crosstab (77/97 rows differ) and per-category distributions. 6) Sensitivity grid 5 filters (F0 all rpp 97; F1 drop==False 90; F2 replicated==1 35; F3 both 31; F4 dedupe repeated titles 95) x 3 junior definitions (D1 AsstProf; D2 +Assistant; D3 +Researcher) x 2 seniority lines, every cell reported as k/N and % with Wilson CIs. 7) Integrity checks: unique ids, no row duplicates, category counts sum to N, D1 subset D2 subset D3, integral F2 counts (10/35, 16/35, 20/35). 8) Confirmatory (not used for numbers): surname-heuristic join of File B project=='Psychology' rows onto rpp (71/73 matched, median |po - p_value.o| = 2.5e-4) to verify that 'Psychology' == project 'rpp'; File B has no seniority field. 9) Descriptive contrast: replication success 16/38 = 42.1% junior-led vs 19/59 = 32.2% senior-led, Fisher exact p = 0.388 (not significant).
